sop_modules.name: Window Painting Setup
sop_modules.description: Floor protection, glass masking, hardware protection, and wall/sill masking. Glass masking is MANDATORY regardless of method. Protection scope varies by application method and adjacent surface state.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Setup
tasks.description: Set up floor protection in window work area. Brush method: drop cloth runners along window perimeter. Spray method: full radial coverage (8 ft radius from each window). Required when floor_type = finished or partial.

quality_notes.all: Brush: runner-style drops along window work perimeter. Spray: full 8 ft radius coverage from each window.

tasks.name: Glass Masking
tasks.description: Apply masking tape and paper/film to all window glass panes. MANDATORY regardless of application method. For wood windows, the 1/16-inch seal technique may apply — paint intentionally overlaps glass by 1/16 inch to create airtight seal (Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1). Multi-pane TDL windows are significantly more labor-intensive.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of all glass panes. Tape edge sealed to frame. Multi-pane (TDL) requires individual pane masking.

tasks.notes: Glass masking is the largest single protection task for window painting. Multi-pane windows take proportionally longer. Liquid masking (Masking Liquid H2O) is an alternative for multi-pane Colonial windows per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.2.

tasks.name: Hardware Protection (Remove or Mask)
tasks.description: Remove or mask window hardware (locks, latches, crank operators, pull handles). Removal preferred when feasible — produces cleaner finish and faster painting. When removal impractical, tape/bag hardware in place.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of all hardware. Removal preferred for clean paint lines around hardware.

tasks.name: Wall Masking Around Window
tasks.description: Apply tape and masking paper at window perimeter to protect wall surface. Required for spray method (always). Also required for brush method when walls are at SS_PAINTED_* state.
tasks.state_condition_note: Spray method: always mask wall around window. Brush method: mask only when walls are SS_PAINTED_* (finished). When walls are SS_PRIMED_FIELD (typical NC), brush method needs no wall masking.

quality_notes.all: Complete tape line around window perimeter. Paper drape for spray, tape-only for brush with finished walls.

tasks.name: Sill/Stool Protection
tasks.description: Tape sill/stool edge to protect from overspray during window spray painting. Only needed when stool is already finished (SS_PAINTED_*) by trim spec.

quality_notes.all: Tape edge along stool top to catch overspray.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Floor protection first, then glass masking (mandatory), then hardware protection, then wall masking (if applicable), then sill protection (if applicable).

sop_modules.name: Window Preparation
sop_modules.description: Substrate-specific preparation. Tasks vary by substrate type (wood, aluminum, steel) and substrate_state (SS_BARE vs SS_PRIMED_FACTORY). Wood SS_BARE: sand, fill, clean. Wood SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: scuff sand, clean. Aluminum: degrease, etch. Steel: degrease, rust treatment.

tasks.name: Sand Bare Wood Windows
tasks.description: Sand bare wood window surfaces (frame, sash, muntins, extension jamb) with 150-220 grit sequence. Follow golden rule: never skip more than one grit. Pre-primer sanding creates tooth for primer adhesion and smooths grain for uniform finish.

quality_notes.QT3: Sand with 150 grit to smooth. Final pass 220 grit on visible surfaces.
quality_notes.QT4: Full sequence 150 → 220 grit. Uniform scratch pattern on all surfaces.
quality_notes.QT5: Full sequence 150 → 220 grit. Uniform scratch pattern. Sand with grain on all surfaces including muntin edges.

tasks.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2. Softwoods (pine, alder): start at 120, finish at 220. Hardwoods (oak, maple): final sand at 150-180 to prevent burnishing.

tasks.name: Fill Defects in Bare Wood
tasks.description: Fill nail holes, grain defects, minor damage on bare wood window surfaces with sandable wood filler. Spot fill only — address visible defects that would telegraph through finish.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill obvious defects — nail holes, deep grain, damage
quality_notes.QT4: Fill all visible defects at 3 feet — nail holes, grain, minor dings
quality_notes.QT5: Fill every defect that could telegraph through finish — complete surface perfection

tasks.name: Scuff Sand Factory Primer
tasks.description: Light scuff sand factory-primed wood window surfaces with 220 grit for mechanical adhesion. Not removing material — creating tooth for finish coat adhesion.

quality_notes.all: Uniform light scratch pattern on all surfaces. Not removing factory primer — creating adhesion tooth.

tasks.name: Degrease Metal Windows
tasks.description: Thorough degreasing of metal window surfaces with alkaline cleaner (BC-7000 or equivalent) to remove oils, greases, and manufacturing residues. MUST precede all mechanical or chemical preparation.

quality_notes.all: Complete degreasing of all surfaces. Water-break test to verify: water sheets evenly with no beading.

tasks.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.1. Always first step for metal substrates.

tasks.name: Chemical Etch / Abrasion — Aluminum
tasks.description: Chemical etch or mechanical abrasion of aluminum window surfaces to remove oxide layer and create adhesion profile for DTM primer. Organofunctional silane or phosphoric acid pre-treatment recommended for maximum adhesion.

quality_notes.all: Uniform etch/abrasion profile on all surfaces. Aluminum oxide layer must be disrupted for primer adhesion.

tasks.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2. Chemical pre-treatment (organofunctional silanes, zirconium/titanium compounds, phosphoric acid) creates chemical bond between metal and paint resin.

tasks.name: Rust Assessment and Treatment — Steel
tasks.description: Assess rust grade per SSPC standards, then treat accordingly. Surface rust: mechanical removal with wire brush/power tool. Scale rust: power tool cleaning + rust converter. Pitting: epoxy fill. Apply rust converter (phosphoric acid) to stabilize surface.

quality_notes.QT3: Remove loose rust and scale. Converter on all exposed steel.
quality_notes.QT4: Thorough rust removal per SSPC-SP3. Converter with complete coverage.
quality_notes.QT5: SSPC-SP11 power tool to bare metal where needed. Full converter treatment. Pit filling with epoxy.

tasks.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.3. Rust grades: Surface (light orange), Scale (flaking layers), Pitting (visible pits), Structural (through-rust — cut out and replace).

tasks.name: Clean Prep Dust and Debris
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust, metal filings, and prep debris from window surfaces with tack cloth. Surface must be clean to touch before primer or finish application.

quality_notes.all: All dust and debris removed. Surface clean to touch. For metal substrates, verify no chemical residue from etch/converter.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Wood SS_BARE: Sand → Fill → Clean. Wood SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: Scuff Sand → Clean. Aluminum: Degrease → Etch → Clean. Steel: Degrease → Rust Treatment → Clean. Only one substrate pathway runs per window.

sop_modules.name: Window Primer Coat
sop_modules.description: Primer coat application. CONDITIONAL: runs only when primer is required. Wood + SS_BARE: acrylic primer (SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC) or shellac spot primer (SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_SHELLAC) for knots/tannin. Aluminum: DTM etching primer (SYS_PRIMER_ALUMINUM_DTM). Steel: rust-inhibitive DTM primer (SYS_PRIMER_STEEL_DTM). Skipped when wood is SS_PRIMED_FACTORY.

applies_when.primer_required_when: substrate_state = SS_BARE (wood) OR substrate = aluminum OR substrate = steel

tasks.name: Brush Primer Coat
tasks.description: Apply primer coat with 1.5-inch angled sash brush (detail work: sash, muntins) and 2-2.5 inch brush (frame faces, extension jamb). Primer type selected by substrate: wood = acrylic, aluminum = DTM etching, steel = rust-inhibitive DTM. For steel: apply immediately after prep to prevent flash rust.

quality_notes.all: Complete uniform coverage. No holidays, drips, or sags. Primer application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.notes: Substrate-driven primer selection per materials.json. All primers are single-coat systems. For wood with knots/tannin bleed, apply SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_SHELLAC spot primer to affected areas before system primer coat.

tasks.name: Spray Primer Coat
tasks.description: Apply primer coat via airless sprayer (310-411 tip). Requires additional masking (wall, sill, extended floor coverage). Primer type selected by substrate.

quality_notes.all: Complete uniform coverage. No holidays, drips, sags, or orange peel. Primer application quality is NOT tiered.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Single primer coat. Primer type driven by substrate — not quality tier. Followed by interstage (inspect, sand, clean) before first finish coat.

sop_modules.name: Window Finish Coat 1
sop_modules.description: First finish coat application. Brush or spray method. Material system driven by quality tier: QT3=SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4=SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5=SYS_FF_PREMIUM. Apply, tip once, walk away — do NOT overwork waterborne products (FFD 15.3.1). BLOCKING PREVENTION: paint sashes in ajar position, do NOT close before full cure (3-7 days for enamels).

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat 1
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat with 1.5-inch angled sash brush (sash, muntins, detail work) and 2-2.5 inch brush (frame faces, extension jamb). Work systematically: frame exterior edges first, then sash, then muntins, then frame interior, then extension jamb. Apply, tip once, walk away — short working time products demand proper first-pass technique (FFD 15.3.1). BLOCKING PREVENTION: paint all operable sashes in ajar position.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Application quality is NOT tiered. If brush marks remain, sand out between coats with rigid block (FFD 15.3.1). Paint sashes AJAR — do NOT close before full cure.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat 1
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat via airless sprayer (310-411 tip). Systematic pass: frame → sash → muntins → extension jamb. Consistent distance and speed for uniform mil thickness. 20-40% material waste from overspray.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. No orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered. Paint sashes AJAR — do NOT close before full cure.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Coat 1 is slower than coat 2 (surface absorption, establishing coverage). Followed by MOD_WIN_INTERSTAGE before coat 2.

sop_modules.name: Window Interstage Process
sop_modules.description: Between-coat maintenance cycle. Inspect, sand, repair, clean. Runs at ALL quality tiers — scrutiny and sanding discipline vary by tier. Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat (FFD 5.3). Applies after primer coat (if applied) and after each finish coat except the last.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat

tasks.name: Inspect Coat
tasks.description: Visual inspection of applied coat on all window surfaces (frame, sash, muntins, extension jamb). Look for dust nibs, brush marks, missed areas, runs, sags, and surface texture issues.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick glance at 6 feet — obvious defects only
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet — mark all visible defects on each surface
quality_notes.QT5: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance on all surfaces including muntin edges

tasks.name: Sand Between Coats
tasks.description: Between-coat sanding on window surfaces. Discipline varies by quality tier. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD 15.4.1). Window sanding is more complex than flat trim — sash profiles, muntin edges, and frame details require careful technique.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot sand only — visible nibs and rough spots. 220 grit.
quality_notes.QT4: Light full sand — entire surface including sash and muntin profiles. 220 grit. Uniform scratch pattern.
quality_notes.QT5: Thorough full sand — entire surface including every muntin edge and profile. 220-320 grit. Uniform scratch pattern. Every imperfection addressed.

tasks.name: Patch/Repair Defects
tasks.description: Fill defects found during inspection. Address issues from previous coat — brush marks, dust nibs, dings.

quality_notes.QT3: Repair only glaring defects — deep scratches, obvious holes
quality_notes.QT4: Repair all marked defects — visible at 3 feet
quality_notes.QT5: Repair all defects regardless of size — anything that could telegraph through finish

tasks.name: Spot Coat Patched Areas
tasks.description: Apply spot coat over patched/repaired areas to build film thickness before next full coat.

quality_notes.QT5: Spot coat all repairs — ensure uniform film build

tasks.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth before next coat application. Critical for dust-free finish on window surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal — surface must be clean to touch before next coat

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Sand Between → Patch Defects (if needed) → Spot Coat (if patched) → Clean Dust. Runs after each coat except the final coat.

sop_modules.name: Window Finish Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Second finish coat application. Faster than coat 1 (consistent substrate). Same application philosophy: apply, tip once, walk away. At QT5 brush/roll, this module may run a third time (3+ coats per FFD 15.10.3). BLOCKING PREVENTION: paint sashes ajar, do NOT close before full cure.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat 2
tasks.description: Apply second finish coat with angled sash brushes. Faster pace than coat 1 — consistent substrate. Same application philosophy: apply, tip once, walk away. BLOCKING PREVENTION: keep sashes ajar.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Application quality is NOT tiered. Paint sashes AJAR.

tasks.notes: Also used for coat 3 at QT5 brush/roll when additional_rounds modifier applies.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat 2
tasks.description: Apply second finish coat via airless sprayer. Faster pace than coat 1 — consistent substrate.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. No orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered. Paint sashes AJAR.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Coat 2 follows interstage. At QT5 brush/roll, this module + interstage may repeat for coat 3 (per round configuration ROUND_WIN_3FINISH).

sop_modules.name: Window Final Inspection and Touch-Up
sop_modules.description: Final quality check and touch-up after last finish coat. Scrutiny varies by quality tier. Verify coverage uniformity, sheen consistency, blocking prevention (sashes ajar), and defect-free finish across all window surfaces.

tasks.name: Final Window Inspection
tasks.description: Final quality check of all painted window surfaces. Verify coverage uniformity, sheen consistency, no runs/sags/holidays, clean glass edges, and sashes positioned ajar for cure.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick glance at 6 feet — no obvious defects, uniform sheen
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet — no visible defects, uniform sheen on frame, sash, and muntins
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance, uniform sheen across all surfaces including muntin edges and jamb

tasks.name: Touch-Up Defects
tasks.description: Address any remaining defects found during final inspection. Touch up with same finish product. Spot sand and recoat as needed.

quality_notes.QT4: Address all visible defects — blend touch-up into surrounding finish
quality_notes.QT5: Address every imperfection — full coat over spot repairs if needed to equalize sheen

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Touch-Up. Runs after the final finish coat (no interstage after this).

sop_modules.name: Window Painting Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Glass scraping, hardware reinstallation, protection teardown, and tool cleanup. Glass scraping occurs AFTER full cure (not between coats) — score paint edge with razor, scrape excess from glass.

tasks.name: Glass Scraping / Cleanup
tasks.description: After full cure: score paint edge on glass with sharp razor blade using putty knife guide for straight lines. Scrape excess paint from glass. Replace razor blades frequently for clean cuts. For 1/16-inch seal technique windows, score precisely at 1/16 inch from frame edge.

quality_notes.all: Clean glass — all excess paint removed. Score line straight and consistent. No scratches on glass from dull blades.

tasks.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1.1. Must wait for full cure before scraping. Multi-pane (TDL) windows take significantly longer. Replace razor blades frequently.

tasks.name: Reinstall Window Hardware
tasks.description: Reinstall removed window hardware (locks, latches, crank operators). Verify operation. If hardware was masked in place, remove masking tape/bags.

quality_notes.all: All hardware reinstalled and operational. No paint on hardware surfaces.

tasks.name: Protection Teardown
tasks.description: Remove all protection materials — floor drops, wall masking, sill masking. Glass masking removed during glass scrape task. Remove tape while finish is still slightly tacky for clean edge.

quality_notes.all: Remove tape at proper time — too early risks smudging, too late risks paint peeling with tape

tasks.notes: Glass masking removed as part of TSK_WIN_GLASS_SCRAPE, not this task. Protection continuity/teardown across specs handled at project level.

tasks.name: Clean Tools
tasks.description: Clean brushes, spray equipment. Proper storage or disposal of consumables.

quality_notes.all: All waterborne products — water cleanup.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Glass scraping (after full cure) → Hardware reinstall → Protection teardown → Clean tools. Glass scraping may happen on a different day than other cleanup tasks due to cure time requirements.

round_configurations.name: Primer + 2-Coat Window Finish
round_configurations.description: Full sequence for SS_BARE windows at QT3/QT4 (all methods) and QT5 spray. Primer coat followed by 2 finish coats with interstage between each.
round_configurations.notes: Primer + 2 finish coats with 2 interstages (after primer, after finish 1). QT5 spray also uses this configuration. Aluminum and steel always use this round since they always require primer.

round_configurations.name: 2-Coat Window Finish (No Primer)
round_configurations.description: Sequence for SS_PRIMED_FACTORY wood windows at QT3/QT4. No primer — scuff sand factory primer then 2 finish coats.
round_configurations.notes: 2 finish coats with 1 interstage between. Prep is scuff sand only. QT5 spray also uses this when SS_PRIMED_FACTORY.

round_configurations.name: 3-Coat Window Finish (QT5 Brush/Roll)
round_configurations.description: Extended coat sequence for QT5 brush/roll per FFD 15.10.3. 3+ coats typical for brush application at gloss sheen. May include primer coat if SS_BARE.
round_configurations.notes: 3 finish coats with interstage between each. If primer included (SS_BARE), total of 4 coats and 3 interstages. Coat 3 uses same rates as coat 2 (consistent substrate). Per human resolution: do NOT enforce spray for QT5 gloss.

assumptions.value: Primer required when substrate_state = SS_BARE (wood) or substrate = aluminum/steel. Skipped when substrate = wood AND substrate_state = SS_PRIMED_FACTORY.
assumptions.source: Window_Systems_Doctrine Sections 3, 6; materials.json primer system applies_when
assumptions.note: Metal substrates always require primer regardless of substrate_state since they need DTM adhesion primer. Wood SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips system primer.

assumptions.value: Interstage process runs after primer coat using the same inspect-sand-repair-clean cycle as between finish coats
assumptions.note: Primer counts as a coat for interstage purposes. After primer cure, inspect primer surface, light sand for adhesion, clean dust before first finish coat.

assumptions.value: Coat 3 at QT5 brush/roll uses same task IDs and rates as coat 2 (TSK_WIN_BRUSH_FINISH_2)
assumptions.source: Aligned with trim paint spec assumption A-002
assumptions.note: No separate coat 3 rates defined. Coat 2 rates apply — substrate is consistent after first coat.

assumptions.value: Glass scraping occurs after full cure (3-7 days for enamels), NOT between coats
assumptions.note: Glass scraping is a cleanup task, not interstage. May happen on a different day than other cleanup tasks.
